title: A snapshot digest

blocks.text: A transit agency's planning service names every scenario's inputs by a digest, so that an auditor can check years later which inputs produced a locked plan. A snapshot is a dict with a `"scenario"` name, `"budgets"` (year strings to $k), `"projects"` (a list of dicts, each with a unique `"pid"`) and `"must_do"` (a list of project ids whose order means nothing). The order of the projects means nothing either.

items: `canonical(snapshot)` returns the snapshot's bytes in one canonical form: the projects sorted by `"pid"`, the must-do ids sorted, then `json.dumps` with sorted keys, separators `(",", ":")` and ASCII only, encoded as UTF-8.
`snapshot_digest(snapshot)` returns the SHA-256 hex digest of those bytes.

blocks.text: Equal content must give equal digests in every process, whatever its string-hash seed, and any change of content a different one. About eight lines.

cases.says: the same content written with its keys in another order gives the same digest, and a $1k change gives another
adding a project changes the digest
the projects listed in another order give the same digest
the must-do ids listed in another order give the same digest
two fresh processes with different string-hash seeds compute the same digest
the digest is taken over exactly the canonical form the statement specifies
